content.text: A proof system is **sound** when everything it proves is valid: if ⊢ φ, then ⊨ φ. Its proofs can be trusted.
Soundness is shown by checking that every rule turns true premises into true conclusions.

examples.title: Soundness stated
lines: ⊨ φ: φ is true in every interpretation.

examples.title: Why it holds
lines: Modus ponens takes true P → Q and true P to Q.
Q is then true as well.
examples.note: A rule that never leads from truth to falsehood keeps proofs safe.

question.prompt: What does it mean for a proof system to be sound?
options: It can prove every valid formula
It never proves a formula that is not valid
question.hint: Soundness is about what the system proves.
question.explanation: Soundness means provability implies validity. The system never proves a formula that is not valid.
